Gauteng Burning - Xenophobia & Looting

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We unpack the story behind the violence plaguing the streets of Johannesburg and Pretoria, and find out why daily looting and pillaging has the province looking like a war zone.

Unique Selling Point:
For the last weeks unprecedented levels of violence and looting have plagued the streets of both Pretoria and Gauteng - we go behind the scenes to find out how the killing of a taxi driver in the pretoria cbd flared into looting and xenophobic attackes

Yunus Salajee Victim

Script:


Voice
From Hillbrow… to Tembisa…, Turfontein…. to Jeppestown, parts of Johannesburg and Pretoria were left resembling a war-zone this week as bullet-casings, burnt out cars and the empty shells of once thriving businesses littered the streets.

Link Devi
It’s been widely reported as further flare ups of xenophobia.

Voice
BUT WHILE XENOPHOBIA MAY HAVE TRIGGERED INITIAL OUTBURSTS OF LOOTING, INNOCENT SHOP OWNERS HAVE BECOME COLLATERAL DAMAGE.
Sarah Motha ADVOCATES FOR Vulnerable Groups at the Foundation for Human Rights – SHE SAYS Scenes of PEOPLE evicted from homes or fleeing their businesses for fear of looting have become commonplace BECAUSE OF A FUNDAMENTAL DISREGARD FOR FOREIGN NATIONALS THAT’S CREPT INTO THE NATIONAL PSYCHE.

Sound Up Sarah Motha
This narrative has become now engrained in the mindset of South Africans, and the disrespect of general migrants, by even politicians, the language that they’ve been using, is as if the other Africans never had anything to do with the democracy that we have today.

Voice
WITH DIVERSE MOTIVES; FROM XENOPHOBIA, TO CRIMINALITY, TO ALLEGATIONS OF A SINISTER THIRD FORCE – LOOTING HAS HAD A DIRE IMPACT ON THOUSANDS OF LIVES. Jules STREET IS one of the worst hit.

Link Devi
Jules street, Johannesburg, very close to the CBD. It’s only when you get here that you understand the true effect of the carnage. But what really confuses me, this is a Pep store, it was looted and burnt. Opposite the road a Shoprite, an attempt was made there too. But you’re talking here about South African brands.

Voice
A few blocks down the road we met Yunus Salajee, a fifth generation South African who has owned a car dealership here for the past 38 years.

Sound Up Yunus
Devi: What happened here?

Yunus: You know, what I can say is, I’m disappointed, I’m not a foreigner and on sunday evening I had a call that there’s problems here. I couldn’t come in the area.

Voice
He was told his vehicles were being broken into and stripped of valuables by gangs of thugs who were looting businesses up and down the road.

Sound Up Yunus
And everything went fine until about half past three in the morning when I had a last call and he says your cars are being lit up.

Voice
Salajee estimates his losses at close to R2.5 million.

Sound Up Yunus
This is people who don’t want to work, but want to steal. It’s the criminals that took advantage about this whole situation.

Voice
Hardware store owner Alan van der Skuif and his shop manager Regina Tsainga APPROACHED US while WE FILMED A BURNED-OUT Liquor outlet.

Sound Up
Regina: They were just stoning cars, attacking everyone, asking everyone where’s you ID? If we didn’t have our ID’s there, they were going to burn us inside there. They were going to burn us. We were crying in there.

Devi: But how do you feel that it’s fellow South Africans that are doing this?

Alan: It’s terrible to think you know that the guys who see me everyday here for 35 years, they know me, they grew up in front of me, that they are the ones who came and steal from me.

Voice
In early August this footage, showing police being chased out of the Johannesburg CBD after attempting to raid shops allegedly selling counterfeit goods, went viral.

Sound Up Sarah Motha
And claiming that these are illegal shops, and they don’t have permits, and that they are holding, and selling or trading in fake goods.

Voice
But the police operation came to a disastrous end when angry mobs went on the rampage. The attacks were mostly blamed on foreign nationals. The following day the cops and Johannesburg Mayor Herman Mashaba were back on the streets to finish the job.

Sound Up Herman Mashaba
We are not going to apologise to anyone for bringing back the rule of law. But at the end of the day, please, make sure that people must understand, we are being failed by Home Affairs. We are being failed by Home Affairs.

Voice
While foreign truck drivers across the country HAVE remained under attack FOR MONTHS, the streets of Johannesburg were relatively calm after that. But a murder in Tshwane last week Tuesday shattered the fragile peace.

Link Devi
Meanwhile, Pretoria was also burning. It was widely reported that there was more examples of xenophobia here, but when you dig a little deeper, a completely different picture emerges.

Voice
The rampage against both foreign and local business owners in the city’s CBD started because of an ongoing war on drugs, according to Piet Mahlangu, Tshwane Chairperson of the National Taxi Alliance. He says drivers at the Dr Savage taxi rank, situated in the middle of a well known hotspot for Nyaw-ope dealers and users, took matters into their own hands after receiving reports that their passengers were being mugged by addicts.

Sound Up Piet Mahlangu
Then the drivers who normally, because they are there all of the time, and some of the operators, decided to say let’s go and chase them away.

Voice
While forcibly removing the addicts from underneath this bridge over the Apies River adjacent to the taxi rank, one of the drivers was shot and killed by an unknown assailant.

Sound Up Mahlangu
Then from there, its then when the drivers came together and said we are tired of this.

Voice
They took to the streets in search of the drug kingpins, many of whom are alleged to be foreign nationals. But the situation spiralled out of control as the taxi drivers were joined by large mobs who burnt down and looted several businesses in the area.
Abner Tsebe is the Tshwane Chairperson of the South African National Taxi Council, and says criminals used the opportunity to run rampant in the streets.

Sound Up Abner Tsebe
This looting, everyone who wants to do it, they must do it aside. Not in our name. And we are coming out strong, we are still going to demonstrate that we are against xenophobic action in our name.

Voice
The Pretoria incident spilled over into renewed violence in Johannesburg. For KENYAN CITIZEN Peter Gakunga, who says he’s invested in South Africa and employs South Africans legally, the attacks amount to pure xenophobia.

Sound Up Peter
Devi: So tell me something, what is the total value that you think you’ve lost?

Peter: Here the total value is over R1,5 million.

Voice
Gakunga owns a car dealership on Jules street, and says he was specifically targeted because he is a foreigner.

Sound Up Peter
We had somebody working for us from South Africa, she told us that she’d heard rumours that they are going to attack foreigners businesses.

Voice
After witnessing the violence, he says he’s now living in fear for his own life.

Sound Peter
What is happening here, another time I think we shall be killed.

Link Devi
The news spread across the continent, and this time fellow Africans were not going to keep quiet. By the end of this week the message was clear, South Africa was not going to get away with it.

Voice
In Nigeria, the South African embassy and a number of South African businesses were closed down as violence flared up in retaliation. Then Zambia AND LATER MALAWI pulled out of international friendlies with Bafana Bafana.

On Tuesday Gauteng Premier David Makhura took to the streets of Johannesburg to try and restore some peace and order.

Sound Up David Makhura
the situation is getting out of hand this side, because two people have been shot.

Voice
The premier said he wouldn’t hesitate to call in the army if the situation got any worse.

Sound Up Makhura
If they can’t cope we will ask the president to ensure that the National Defence Force reinforces them, but so far it’s not necessary.

Voice
President Cyril Ramaphosa said he had instructed the minister of police to meet community leaders and put an end to the violence.

Sound Up Cyril Ramaphosa
Because this violence is now mutating and taking different forms, that represent themselves in a way that we do not want to see in South Africa where communities seem to be attacking one another. So we want this to stop.

Voice
In total, ten people have reportedly died in the violence to date, and while the streets had calmed down by thursday, the situation remained tense. The taxi bosses in Tshwane have called off any further protests from their members. They say their war on drugs will continue, but instead of taking matters into their own hands, they’ll be working with law enforcement.

Sound Up Mahlangu
We really apologise to what happened to some of the people, because they are not drug dealers. But we also say, we will not stop at any moment where we see the Nyaope, we will deal with them.


Promo 1
Voice
We examine the aftermath of a new wave of xenophobic violence that’s ruined lives, cost millions and left the streets of Johannesburg and Pretoria ablaze.

Promo 2
Voice
Johannesburg and Pretoria resembled an outright war zone over the past few weeks - we examine the complex reasons behind the chaos and destruction.

Promo 3
Voice
A war on drugs, the murder of a taxi driver and looting and pillaging on a grand scale - we explore some of the issues around the latest xenophobic attacks.
